solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Tycoon in Asian river experiment is German (13)

annotation.surface: A business magnate conducting some experiment on an Asian river, with a German involved.
annotation.walkthrough: 'is German' reads as a statement about nationality; it is an instruction to put 'is' into German.
annotation.definitionFit: An industrialist is a tycoon who owns or runs industry.

entries.clue: Just beginning nice pint I ordered (9)

indicatorNotes.ordered: the letters are put in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone who has only just started drinking orders a nice pint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a pub order being placed; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Something incipient is in its first stage, just beginning.

entries.clue: Corrupt fellow holding record on river (7)

indicatorNotes.holding: DAVE holds the other letters inside him
indicatorNotes.on: in a down entry, EP sits on top of R

blocks.note: any man's name will do for 'fellow'

annotation.surface: A crooked man with a record, living by a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'record' suggests a criminal record, fitting the corrupt fellow; it is a gramophone record.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean making someone morally worse, leading them into wickedness.

entries.clue: Sparkle misplaced in Tallis etc (11)

indicatorNotes.misplaced: the letters are put in the wrong places, so rearranged

annotation.surface: A remark that sparkle is out of place in the sober church music of Thomas Tallis and his like.
annotation.walkthrough: Thomas Tallis was a Tudor composer of church music, so the surface reads as music criticism; 'etc' is needed only for its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean giving off flashes of light, and both extend to lively, brilliant conversation.

entries.clue: Secluded place for a break (6)

blocks.note: second meaning: a pause, as in a school or parliamentary break

annotation.surface: Advice to find a quiet spot for a holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses are nouns: a nook in a wall and a pause in business.
annotation.definitionFit: A recess is both a secluded alcove and a break from work.

entries.clue: Fawning grown-up penning article on Scottish island mostly (9)

indicatorNotes.penning: ADULT pens, or encloses, the article
indicatorNotes.on: in a down entry, the first part sits on top of the second
indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: IONA, the Hebridean island, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A grown-up writing a flattering article about a Scottish island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'penning' reads as writing an article; here it means enclosing one, as in a sheep pen.
annotation.definitionFit: Adulation is excessive admiration, the fawning of a flatterer.

entries.clue: Uncompromising senior officer being conveyed around (12)

indicatorNotes.around: the conveyed phrase goes around the officer

blocks.note: goods being conveyed are in transit

annotation.surface: A stubborn senior officer being driven about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'senior officer' is so in keeping with 'uncompromising' that it seems part of the definition; it is only three letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Intransigent means refusing to compromise.

entries.clue: Pouring rain let rot spread (10)

indicatorNotes.spread: the letters are spread about into a new order

annotation.surface: Heavy rain has let rot spread through the house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pouring rain' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Pouring' and 'rain' is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent flood of water, so a downpour heavy enough to resemble one is described this way.

entries.clue: Bloke securing drink knocked back by Irish singer (9)

indicatorNotes.securing: BOD holds the other letters inside
indicatorNotes.knocked back: a drink knocked back is drunk, and here also turned back

blocks.note: bod is informal for a person

annotation.surface: A man holding a drink he downs while an Irish singer performs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Irish singer' reads as one person; 'Irish' is two letters and 'singer' alone is the bird.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this Australasian bird, famous for decorating its courtship bower, is a songbird, and crosswords often call any bird a singer.

entries.clue: Express disapproval of king’s literary work (4)

annotation.surface: A critic jeering at a king's writings.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: novels, memoirs and poetry collections all get published as bound volumes.

entries.clue: Town with Welshman spreading danger: extremely canny about it (6,6,4)

indicatorNotes.spreading: DANGER is spread into a new order
indicatorNotes.extremely: only the extremes, the first and last letters
indicatorNotes.about: about means surrounding, so the outer letters C and Y go around IT

annotation.surface: A town where a Welshman spreads danger, with some shrewd observation about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a joining word but is W. Welwyn Garden City is a planned town in Hertfordshire, north of London.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: it is a planned settlement in Hertfordshire, founded in 1920 under Ebenezer Howard's movement.

entries.clue: Discharge explosive substance in Hebridean island (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the explosive goes in the island

blocks.note: Rum is an island in the Inner Hebrides

annotation.surface: An order to set off explosives on a Scottish island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' suggests firing, fitting the explosive; here it is a bodily discharge, a watery mucus.
annotation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose.

entries.clue: Cool drink, we hear, for one in the know (7)

indicatorNotes.we hear: the words are taken as heard, not as spelt

blocks.note: cider is a drink made from apples

annotation.surface: A chilled drink recommended by someone well informed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cool drink' reads as a chilled drink; 'Cool' is IN, a separate word from the drink.
annotation.definitionFit: An insider is someone with inside knowledge, one in the know.

entries.clue: Skilful person given post covering Republican rally (13)

indicatorNotes.covering: STATION covers, or goes around, the R

blocks.note: a demon at something is very good at it
a post or station of duty

annotation.surface: A capable person gets a job looking after a Republican rally.
annotation.walkthrough: 'rally' sits at the end looking like part of the political story; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are mass public gatherings held to protest or show support for a cause.

entries.clue: Surpass American state and European island (5)

annotation.surface: A travel boast about outdoing an American state and a European island.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue seems to list three things; the last two words are the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples.

entries.clue: Bar key painting? That’s a slip (11)

blocks.note: the counter of a pub or shop

annotation.surface: A painting hung behind a pub bar is said to be a mistake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'slip' suggests an error; it is a slip of paper.
annotation.definitionFit: A counterfoil is the slip kept as a record when a cheque or ticket is torn off.

entries.clue: Racecourse record thus misrepresented at first (5)

annotation.surface: A racecourse's record has been misrepresented from the start.
annotation.walkthrough: Epsom Downs in Surrey is the course where the Derby is run.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Surrey downs host the Derby and the Oaks, two classic horse races.

entries.clue: Quiet Hampshire arts master disturbed by a ghostly vision (9)

indicatorNotes.disturbed by: HANTS is broken into by the A

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation of the English county

annotation.surface: A quiet arts master from Hampshire is shaken by a ghost.
annotation.walkthrough: The ghost story hides that 'disturbed' interrupts the county abbreviation rather than scrambling it: HANTS keeps its order around the A.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the Greek-derived word names an apparition or illusion, something seen that is not really there.

entries.clue: The last word in armaments! (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer is found inside the next word

blocks.note: the letters run consecutively inside this word

annotation.surface: An advertising slogan for the latest weapons.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The last word in' reads as 'the very latest in', an advertising cliché; it splits into the definition and a hidden-word indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Amen is the word said at the end of a prayer.

entries.clue: Hired ruffian’s year stalking male cricketer (8)

indicatorNotes.stalking: the year follows the male, as a stalker follows

blocks.note: mid-on is a fielding position in cricket, and so the fielder there

annotation.surface: A thug spent a year stalking a cricketer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'stalking' fits the ruffian's menace but only puts YR after M.
annotation.definitionFit: A myrmidon is a hired thug who carries out orders without scruple.

entries.clue: Half-hearted boost popular with old Asian islander (8)

indicatorNotes.Half-hearted: the heart of FILLIP is LL; half of it goes

blocks.note: FILLIP (a boost) with one of its two central Ls removed

annotation.surface: A feeble attempt at encouragement that went down well with an old Asian.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' sounds like 'lacklustre'; here it removes half of the middle, one L of the double L.
annotation.definitionFit: A Filipino is a native of the Philippines, an island nation in Asia.

entries.clue: Cleric entering cathedral city in a calm manner (6)

indicatorNotes.entering: the cleric goes inside the city

blocks.note: Venerable, the title of an archdeacon
Ely in Cambridgeshire, the crossword's favourite cathedral city

annotation.surface: A clergyman arriving calmly in a cathedral city.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition reads as the manner of the cleric's entry; it is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: To speak evenly is to speak in a calm, level manner.

entries.clue: Very early way to keep trees: get your priorities right (5,6,5)

indicatorNotes.to keep: ST keeps the trees inside it

annotation.definitionNote: The answer is a saying and the definition an instruction; the phrase is used as that very instruction.
annotation.surface: Advice to get up very early to protect the trees, and so get priorities straight.
annotation.walkthrough: The FIRST in FIRS is disguised as trees rather than as the word first, so the repetition in the answer never shows in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Saying 'first things first' urges dealing with the most important matters before others.

entries.clue: Blowout in tyre ultimately disturbing at speed (5)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of tyre is used
indicatorNotes.disturbing: the E interrupts FAST, breaking into it

annotation.surface: A tyre bursting while the car is travelling fast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blowout' in a sentence about tyres means a burst; its other sense is a big meal.
annotation.definitionFit: A blowout is informal for a lavish meal, a feast.

entries.clue: Old county councillors initially want luxury food and new horse (16)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of councillors is used

blocks.note: manna, heaven-sent food, used loosely for any delicacy
the shire is a heavy draught horse

annotation.surface: A council in an old county wants fine food and a new horse.
annotation.walkthrough: Clackmannanshire is a small historic county in central Scotland; 'Old' is needed because it was merged away in 1975 before being revived as a council area.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Scotland's smallest historic shire, abolished as a county in 1975 and later revived as a council area.

entries.clue: Waterproof fabric a Republican chap stored in container (9)

indicatorNotes.stored in: the letters are put inside the container

annotation.surface: A Republican wrapped in waterproof sheeting and packed in a box.
annotation.walkthrough: 'container' does double duty in the surface as the storage box, but in the wordplay it supplies TIN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tarred or coated canvas, sheeted over lorries and boats to keep rain out.

entries.clue: Like part of organ in later reconstruction? (7)

indicatorNotes.reconstruction: the letters are rebuilt in a new order

annotation.surface: A question about organ parts in a later rebuilding, as of a church organ.
annotation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the musical instrument being rebuilt; the organ is the eye.
annotation.definitionFit: Retinal means relating to the retina, part of the eye.

entries.clue: Craftsman finally becoming less active (7)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter of becoming is used

annotation.surface: A tradesman who, in the end, is slowing down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'finally' sits after 'Craftsman', seeming to describe him, but it selects from 'becoming'.
annotation.definitionFit: A glazier is a craftsman who fits glass.

entries.clue: Brightest star principally associated with sacred river (5)

indicatorNotes.principally: principally means chiefly, first of all, so only the opening letter of associated is used

blocks.note: Alph is the sacred river of Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan

annotation.surface: The brightest star is chiefly linked with a holy river.
annotation.walkthrough: Stars in a constellation are lettered by the Greek alphabet, the brightest usually first; 'principally' seems to qualify the star but picks a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Alpha is the name given to the brightest star in a constellation.

entries.clue: Thoughtful writers originally illustrating victory in Europe (7)

indicatorNotes.originally: originally means at the origin, so only the opening letter of illustrating is used

blocks.note: the initials, as in VE Day, 8 May 1945

annotation.surface: Reflective authors first depicted the victory in Europe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'victory in Europe' is the full phrase for VE; 'writers' are pens rather than authors.
annotation.definitionFit: Pensive means deep in thought.

entries.clue: Cutting off chaps in army corps needing time to cross ditch (12)

indicatorNotes.to cross: the soldiers' letters straddle the ditch, lying either side of it

annotation.surface: Soldiers crossing a ditch against the clock, with some of them cut off.
annotation.walkthrough: The chaps are men in the army corps, so RE comes first; RE, MEN and T then cross, or span, the ditch.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names a reduction of costs or staff, the cutting away of expenditure an organisation can spare.

entries.clue: Athletic little chap crossing sierra: seamstresses may use it (7,6)

indicatorNotes.crossing: loose: the little chap is pictured crossing a sierra, and S is set at his front

blocks.note: S in the NATO phonetic alphabet
titch is British slang for a small person

annotation.surface: A sporty small man trekking over a mountain range, with a note about sewing.
annotation.walkthrough: A titch is a small person in British slang. The definition is a description, not a synonym: running stitch is the basic in-and-out stitch.
annotation.definitionFit: Running stitch is a simple line of stitches, a staple of sewing.

entries.clue: Month attorney finally framed acceptable system of rule (8)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter of attorney is used

annotation.surface: An attorney at last framed an acceptable system of government this month.
annotation.walkthrough: 'framed' suggests a lawyer drafting or setting someone up; here the month is a frame around ON.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: government headed by a hereditary king or queen is one form of state organisation.

entries.clue: Female Latvian opposed to dabblers (10)

annotation.surface: A Latvian woman who disapproves of amateurs.
annotation.walkthrough: Lett is an old word for a Latvian, the key to the clue; the answer is the Italian plural.
annotation.definitionFit: Dilettanti are amateurs who dabble in the arts.

entries.clue: Doctor coped nicely, given a reference book (12)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor is to tamper with, so rearrange

annotation.surface: A doctor who managed well when handed a medical reference work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' sits at the front looking like a person; it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a compendium of articles covering general knowledge, consulted rather than read through.

entries.clue: Failure to settle on mat Penny repaired (10)

indicatorNotes.repaired: the letters are mended into a new order

annotation.surface: Penny mended a mat but has not settled the bill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'settle' reads as sitting on the mat; it means paying a bill.
annotation.definitionFit: To settle a bill is to pay it, so neglecting what is owed is exactly this default.

entries.clue: Caustic account delivered (5)

annotation.surface: A scathing report has been handed in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'account delivered' reads as a report given; the sense of 'delivered' is set free.
annotation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharp or biting, caustic.

entries.clue: Fashionable inference to finish with (2,10)

annotation.surface: A trendy deduction to round things off.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an adverbial phrase; 'to finish with' works as 'finally', which is what 'in conclusion' means.
annotation.definitionFit: Both phrases are used by speakers signalling their closing remark, meaning lastly or finally.

entries.clue: Like protozoans, extremely unusual in college wine store (11)

indicatorNotes.extremely: only the extremes, first and last letters
indicatorNotes.in: those letters go inside the wine store

annotation.surface: Microbes turning up, most unusually, in a college wine cellar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'extremely unusual' reads as 'very odd'; it gives just U and L.
annotation.definitionFit: Protozoans are single-celled organisms, so unicellular.

entries.clue: Common rite broadcast strictly in time (10)

annotation.surface: A common service transmitted on air with strict timing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests a radio service, but it is seed scattered, the letters thrown about.
annotation.definitionFit: Metronomic means as regular as a metronome, strictly in time.

entries.clue: Comparatively inactive fish seen round lake and river (5)

indicatorNotes.round: the fish goes round the lake

blocks.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: A sluggish fish spotted near a lake and a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is the comparative adjective, more idle, not the noun for a layabout.
annotation.definitionFit: Idler is the comparative of idle, meaning less active.

entries.clue: Nanny trains where plants are reared (7)

blocks.note: a nanny is a children's nurse

annotation.surface: A nanny who trains children, and plants brought up like them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nanny trains' sets up child-rearing, and a nursery is also where children are reared, but the definition is the garden kind.
annotation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where young plants are raised for sale.

entries.clue: Unacceptable corollaries for mounted escorts (9)

blocks.note: a rider is an added clause or corollary

annotation.surface: A logician's objection to extra propositions about mounted guards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'corollaries' is the hard step: a rider is an addendum following from what went before.
annotation.definitionFit: Outriders are escorts on horses or motorcycles riding beside a vehicle.

entries.clue: Odd in Scotland, keeping box for players (9)

indicatorNotes.keeping: ORRA keeps the box inside it

blocks.note: orra is Scots for odd or spare

annotation.surface: A strange Scottish custom of keeping a box for musicians.
annotation.walkthrough: 'box' suggests a box at the theatre, where players are watched; it is a chest.
annotation.definitionFit: The players here are musicians, and a large ensemble of strings, wind and percussion performing together is this.

entries.clue: Charming woman taking uniform from supply on ship (9)

indicatorNotes.taking: taking in the sense of removing, as in taking one number away from another
indicatorNotes.from: the U is taken out of SOURCE

blocks.note: U in the NATO phonetic alphabet, removed

annotation.surface: An attractive woman takes a uniform from the ship's stores.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charming' means casting charms, not pleasant; 'on' is RE, about.
annotation.definitionFit: A sorceress is a woman who casts spells, literally charming.

entries.clue: Old timer’s impressive face captivating stout woman (11,5)

indicatorNotes.captivating: GRAND and CLOCK capture the stout woman between them

annotation.surface: An old man's striking face charms a stout woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old timer' looks like an old man; it is a timepiece. 'impressive face' splits in two, with the woman held between.
annotation.definitionFit: Timer means timepiece, and this tall pendulum longcase piece is traditionally antique, hence old.

entries.clue: What racing tipster is in relation to starting price (7)

annotation.definition: What racing tipster is in relation to starting price

blocks.note: the surface reading: a horse-racing tipster and the starting price of a horse
the setter's reading: the letters of 'racing tipster' and 'starting price' are the same, rearranged

annotation.surface: A question about how a racing tipster's advice relates to a horse's starting odds.
annotation.walkthrough: At the racecourse the starting price is a horse's final odds. Count the letters: RACING TIPSTER and STARTING PRICE are the same thirteen.
annotation.definitionFit: Each phrase is a rearrangement of the other.

entries.clue: Restore theatre before broadcast (6)

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

annotation.surface: A theatre is being refurbished before a broadcast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like an anagram indicator; here it is simply AIR.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean mending something damaged back to working condition.

entries.clue: Way to enter a bridle path, seated thus? (7)

indicatorNotes.to enter: the way goes inside A RIDE

blocks.note: a ride is a track for horse riding

annotation.surface: A horse rider asks how to get onto a bridle path, and how to sit.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: on a bridle path you sit astride your horse.
annotation.definitionFit: Astride is the posture of a rider, a leg either side.

entries.clue: Robber’s daughter taking vermouth, propping up bar (6)

indicatorNotes.taking: taking in the sense of having a drink, so the daughter is followed by her vermouth
indicatorNotes.propping up: in a down entry, D and IT go below the bar, holding it up

blocks.note: Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

annotation.surface: A thief's daughter drinking vermouth while leaning on a bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'propping up the bar' is a pub idiom for drinking; here 'bar' is BAN and the rest sits under it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an outlaw who steals, often by ambushing travellers on remote roads.

entries.clue: Note about wild partygoers makes us cross (8)

indicatorNotes.about: the note goes about, or around, the partygoers

blocks.note: te, the seventh note in tonic sol-fa

annotation.surface: A complaint about noisy revellers that makes us angry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'cross' means angry in the surface; the definition is the verb, to go across.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean travelling over or through something from one side to the other.

entries.clue: English chap rejecting mother’s code of beliefs (5)

indicatorNotes.rejecting: MA is thrown out of the chap's name

annotation.surface: An Englishman who turns his back on his mother's values.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is a link, not a possessive; the name is chosen because removing MA leaves THOS.
annotation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit and beliefs of a group.

entries.clue: Photograph game (4)

blocks.note: second meaning: the card game where matching cards are called

annotation.walkthrough: Snap is a simple children's card game in which players shout when two matching cards appear.
annotation.definitionFit: One noun, two senses: an informal quick picture taken with a camera, and a children's cards contest won by shouting first.

entries.clue: Eastern girl’s shoulder piece (9)

annotation.surface: A girl from the East and her shoulder ornament.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possession but is the link 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the ornamental strap or pad worn on each side of a military uniform, often marking rank.

entries.clue: Breeding establishment set at last in south of France (4)

indicatorNotes.at last: at last means at the end, so only the closing letter of set is used
indicatorNotes.in: in places the T inside the French word, between S and UD

annotation.surface: A stud farm set up at last in the south of France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'south of France' reads as the region; it asks for the French word for south.
annotation.definitionFit: A stud is an establishment where horses are kept for breeding.

entries.clue: Set fire to church by rocky peak (5)

indicatorNotes.by: the church stands by, after, the peak

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

annotation.surface: An arsonist's instruction to burn a church beside a crag.
annotation.walkthrough: A tor is a craggy hilltop in the south-west of England.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: informal verb for deliberately burning a building or vehicle, as an arsonist does.

entries.clue: Stylish fellow I arranged to meet — and terrorised! (11)

blocks.note: to date is to arrange to meet

annotation.surface: A smart man I agreed to meet turned out to be frightening.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash and 'and' mark a twist in the story; the dating reads as romance but gives DATED.
annotation.definitionFit: To intimidate is to frighten or terrorise.

entries.clue: River, one featuring in folk legend (5)

indicatorNotes.featuring in: the one appears inside the legend

annotation.surface: A river that appears in a folk tale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'folk legend' reads as a legendary person; it is the stories themselves, lore.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: France's longest waterway, flowing past chateaux to the Atlantic at Nantes.

entries.clue: Leader limiting a politician’s time in N London suburb (9)

indicatorNotes.limiting: HEAD limits, or encloses, the rest

annotation.surface: A party leader curbing an MP's time in a London suburb.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's here does give letters: MP'S keeps its S. Hampstead is a leafy, well-off area of north London.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the hilly, affluent district beside the Heath, within the borough of Camden.

entries.clue: Lacking individuality, unlike Hamlet for example (13)

blocks.note: second meaning read literally: Hamlet is a character, so what is unlike him is less a character

annotation.surface: A remark that something bland is nothing like Shakespeare's Hamlet.
annotation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: Hamlet is a character, so anything unlike him is 'character-less'.
annotation.definitionFit: Characterless means lacking distinctive qualities.
